s-05-4-correct.alt: Ten interface states on Newsprint, labeled Illustrative, each with a sample and its cue: Hover: The fill steps from Charcoal to Prussian and the label underlines. Focus: A 2 px Verdigris ring with a 2 px gap, shown at once. Disabled: A dashed edge, readable text and a line that says what makes it available. Loading: A still outline and the words that say what is loading. Selected: The paired surface, a 4 px bar and a check. Muted: Regular weight and an outline mark. Warning: A triangle, the word Warning and a 4 px bar. Warning has no hue of its own. Error: The word Error, a glyph and the fix in plain words, on the Error Band. Empty: A dashed region that says what is missing and what to do next. Success: A Verdigris check and a word such as Saved.

s-11-2-correct.alt: The six states of a step, each drawn on step 4 at true size and at twice size, with its name and meaning. Done: The step happened. Now: The bill is at this step, and the words beside the tracker name it. You can take part now: The bill is at this step, and the public can act before a date. The red disc, its place on the ring and the words carry it together. Not yet: The bill has not reached this step. Never happened: The bill moved past this step without it, as when a committee votes without holding a hearing. It keeps its number, so the count still runs to six. Stopped: The bill ended here, as when a committee votes it down or a veto stands. The line ends at this step. Done is a filled circle; Now is a heavy ring; You can take part now is the heavy ring with a small red disc at its upper right; Not yet is a fine ring; Never happened is the fine ring under a slash; Stopped is a filled square.

s-11-steps.alt: The six steps, with what happens at each. 1, Filed: A legislator files the bill, and it goes to a committee. 2, Hearing: The committee holds a hearing and takes testimony on the bill. Many state legislatures take testimony from the public there. In Congress, the committee hears the witnesses it invites. A bill’s own page says how to take part. 3, Committee vote: The committee votes on whether to send the bill to the full House or Senate. 4, First chamber: The full House or Senate, wherever the bill was filed, votes on it. 5, Second chamber: The other chamber takes the bill up. Its own committee can hold a hearing first, and then the full chamber votes and both chambers agree on one text. 6, Governor or President: The governor signs a state bill and the President signs a federal one. Either can veto it, and lawmakers can vote to override a veto.
